name: pwntools
desc: CTF framework used by Gallopsled in every CTF
why: A CTF exploitation framework that opens a door into binary exploitation and running programs.

brief.what_it_is: Pwntools is a CTF framework and exploit development library written in Python. You import it into a Python script (the README example starts with `from pwn import *`), set a target context such as architecture and OS, open a connection to a remote service, and send it payloads. It can also assemble and disassemble code, including shellcode generated by its shellcraft module. It ships about 19 command-line tools alongside the library, including asm, checksec, cyclic, disasm, elfpatch, shellcraft, template and unhex.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a CTF framework and exploit development library designed for rapid prototyping, "intended to make exploit writing as simple as possible."
brief.how_it_works: Everything is driven from Python: a script imports the pwn package, configures context(arch, os), and uses helpers such as remote() to talk to a target, asm() and shellcraft to produce machine code, and interactive() to hand control to the user. Most functionality is self-contained Python, but assembling and disassembling foreign architectures calls out to non-Python binutils-style dependencies.

brief.install_notes: Installed via pip (PyPI package pwntools), not brew alone. Best supported on 64-bit Ubuntu LTS (22.04 and 24.04 per the README; the docs page still lists older 14.04 through 20.04). Requires Python 3.10+ since version 5.0.0; use 4.x for Python 2.7 or older Pythons. Some features, notably assembling and disassembling foreign architectures, need non-Python dependencies such as binutils and cmake/pkg-config on macOS. If installed as an unprivileged user, the command-line tools land in ~/.local/bin, which must be added to PATH. No account or hardware is needed.
brief.standout: It turns exploit scripting into a short Python idiom: a few lines connect to a remote host, generate shellcode with shellcraft, and drop into an interactive shell. The bundled CLI tools (checksec, cyclic, elfpatch and others) cover the rest of the binary-exploitation toolbox in one install.
brief.status: Maintained. The README links to a current docs site (version 4.15.0 shown on the install docs page), a CI badge on the dev branch, a PyPI badge, and a Discord. I did not see a release date or last commit date in the fetched pages, so the exact recency is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: Python 2.7 is no longer supported in 5.x; the docs say Python 2 is deprecated. Foreign-architecture assembly and disassembly need extra system packages. Official support centres on 64-bit Ubuntu LTS, with other Posix systems described as 'most functionality should work'. The README calls it a CTF framework, so it is aimed at exploit work rather than general-purpose binary analysis. The MIT license is noted in the badges.
quotes: Pwntools is a CTF framework and exploit development library. Written in Python, it is designed for rapid prototyping and development, and intended to make exploit writing as simple as possible.
Most of the functionality of pwntools is self-contained and Python-only.
